_comment: Bean d5f1. One agent's INSPECTION of every extracted image, as data rather than code, so the judgement can be reviewed line by line and re-run. `saw` is the REASON for the role, not the description; `draft` is the description. EVERY ENTRY HERE WAS PRODUCED BY OPENING THE IMAGE -- all fifty, one at a time. Applied by scripts/apply-image-verdicts.ts, which writes an `inspection` basis naming this agent and leaves every narrative in `draft`: only a human may confirm one (schemas/narrative.ts). THIS DOCUMENT IS WHY `placements[]` EXISTS (bean j820, issue #1234). It was staged with 383 entries and read as 383 images; it holds FIFTY, several placed a dozen or more times. The first reading of it -- 'fragments of one composite architecture figure', 'many byte-identical in size', '383 descriptions would be fabrication' -- was wrong on all three counts, inferred from file sizes rather than from looking. Fifty descriptions is ordinary work and this is it. FIVE ARE `logo` RATHER THAN `figure`: the Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Wikipedia marks are somebody's trademark used as a stock glyph, and saying so tells a reader they are not content the authors drew. The PDF glyph is generic and stays `figure`.

img-p002-1.saw: a line-art human figure, the asker in the example exchange
img-p002-1.draft: A black line-art icon of a person: a circle for the head above a rounded torso. It marks the human's turn in the worked example on this page, where a user asks a question about an insurance brochure.

img-p002-10.saw: a page of the insurance brochure the example questions
img-p002-10.draft: A page from a Prudential Singapore brochure headed "PRUShield Premier and PRUExtra Supplementary Plans: Coverage for private hospital not under Prudential's Panel and Non-Panel listings". It works through one scenario -- a private hospital single-bedded ward, total bill S$80,000 -- showing what PRUShield Premier covers (S$68,850, John pays S$11,150) and then four supplementary options beneath it, each with its daily premium and what John would still pay: PRUExtra Premier CoPay (S$5,900, with a level-progression bar advancing him to Level 4), PRUExtra Preferred CoPay (S$11,150), and PRUExtra Premier Lite CoPay (S$7,325).

img-p002-11.saw: a two-cell extract from the brochure's comparison table
img-p002-11.draft: A two-cell strip lifted from the brochure's comparison table. The left cell reads "PRUShield's deductible amount for claims not under panel providers (Per policy year)"; the right reads "Covers 95% of deductible amount that is above S$2,000, you pay S$2,000 and 5% of the remaining deductible amount". It is the row the worked example's answer is drawn from.

img-p002-12.saw: the brochure's full plan-comparison table, a full page
img-p002-12.draft: A full brochure page headed "A little extra goes a long way", holding a dense comparison table of five supplementary plans across two PRUShield tiers -- PRUExtra Premier CoPay, Preferred CoPay, Premier Lite CoPay, Plus CoPay and Plus Lite CoPay. Rows cover hospital and ward types, cancer drug treatment and services, deductible handling under and outside panel providers, co-insurance, stop-loss, claims-based premium pricing, value-added services, premiums for a 30-year-old (S$832.80 down to S$158.00) and eligibility. Ten numbered footnotes run beneath it.
